title: Designing a Robust Avatar Component System
summary: This lesson outlines best practices for creating flexible avatar components, including fallback strategies and deterministic coloring. It covers visual consistency through limited sizing and integrated status indicators to reduce UI clutter.

transcript.text: The photo fails, the avatar shouldn't.
Image first, initials when it fails. A generic icon as a last resort. Never a broken square.
Generate the background color from the name itself. Same person, same color, on every screen, forever. No random palette.
Two initials by default: first name, last name. Drop to a single letter only at tiny sizes. JD reads as a person, a lone J reads as a bug.
Overlap them to show a group. Cap the row and spill the rest into a plus three.
A ring around the avatar shows who's online. Put the status on the ring, never a second badge.
Pick three sizes and stop. 24 in lists, 32 in headers, 40 in profiles. Three tokens, nothing between.
More UI systems at designmotionhq.com. Link in bio, save this for your next component.

on_screen_text: One image fails? Degrade, don't break.
Two letters read as a person.
Overlap the group, cap the row.
before_after: Transitions from broken image icons to a fallback chain, random colors to name-based colors, and redundant badges to integrated status rings.
